subject: ventures/buymeacoffee-payout-to-journal
professional: a bookkeeper (QuickBooks ProAdvisor / Xero Advisor) who keeps books for several online creators, checking first that gross income, fees and clearing balance and tie to the PayPal/Stripe deposit, then that the import files load

evidence.correctness: Ran node /scratchpad script against calc.mjs with a hand-built 4-row export that straddles a month end (values I chose, not the author's sample): Jan row Given 1,200.00 / Received 1,141.50 gave donations credit 1200.00, fees debit 58.50, clearing debit 1141.50 (matches hand arithmetic 1200-58.50); Feb rows (10/9.35, 120/112.10, 18/16.75) gave credits 10/120/18, fees debit 9.80 (0.65+7.90+1.25), clearing 138.20 (=9.35+112.10+16.75). Both journals balance; two journals produced for the month split, last dated at the last row's date. Thousands-separator amounts ('1,141.50') parsed right. Xero amounts debit-positive/credit-negative and IIF TRNS/SPL signs match the published import conventions as I know them. Refund recomputation (Given 10, Received 0, refunded=true plus a normal row) gave donations 20.00 cr, refunds 10.00 dr, fees 1.00 dr, clearing 9.00: correct. Limit: fee booked as one line, no split of BMC cut vs processor, and the export layout itself is unverified, so correctness is of the model, not of a real export.
evidence.completeness: README/VENTURE/page claims checked and worked in a run: TransactionType income split (donation/subscription/shop/commission) works; fee = Given - Received works; deposit proof via opts.expected works; month split works; Xero, QBO, IIF and plain CSV builders all emit output; uncategorised never dropped (Gift Card -> uncategorised); mapping editor parseMapping exists. 37 tests pass. Stage is 'prototype' and the hypothesis is untested; no real BMC export or live import ever ran, which the page admits. Nothing found stubbed.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/buymeacoffee-payout-to-journal && node --test '*.test.mjs': 37 pass, 0 fail. Mutation 1: changed the deposit check `s.stated !== sum` to `s.stated > sum` in buildJournals: 1 test failed (#7, broken sample names the mismatch). Mutation 2: forced `derived = false` (fee derivation off): 5 tests failed (1, 4, 7, 8, 10). Both reverted from a backup copy; git status clean. Weakness: the 'stated < sum' direction (rows exceed deposit) is covered only by the one broken-sample test, and incomeCategory has no test for overlapping keywords (see defects).
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (all 380 lines), page.test.mjs, calc.test.mjs header. Integer cents throughout, no DOM/network in calc, pure functions, findings with severities, never drops rows. Defects: incomeCategory tests 'support' and 'coffee' before 'member'/'commission' so 'Membership support' and 'Coffee commission' land in donations; item alias list repeats "item"; the shop regex includes generic 'order'/'extra'; parsePayouts is one 100-line function mixing parse, fee derivation and tax logic; fee/tax/refund heuristics (taxInNet, refund residual into fees) are guesses with no real data behind them. Silent-ish fallback: a blank type is treated as donation.
evidence.claims: Backed: no-upload claim (page.test asserts no fetch/XHR; grep confirms none), disclaimer and financial-data clause present (index.html:134,136), 'read from memory' unverified caveat in README, VENTURE.yaml and page. Not backed or inconsistent: (1) index.html FAQ says 'sales tax or VAT collected on shop orders is not separated from the fee and income' but calc.mjs has a tax category and taxInNet logic that does separate it when columns exist; (2) llms.txt links the old github.io address instead of https://marisstella.app/buymeacoffee-payout-to-journal/ (the live address in README/VENTURE); (3) robots.txt 'Sitemap: ./sitemap.xml' is a relative URL, which robots.txt does not allow; (4) README's 'After using this, you can now book ... proven against your deposit' is stated as an outcome although nothing ran on a real export; the page does hedge this in the note. Also the README test command path runs from repo root only.
evidence.fitness: Walked a creator's job: paste CSV, type PayPal deposit, pick format, download Xero/QBO/IIF. Works on files shaped like the assumed header (DateTime, Received, Given, TransactionType). The real BMC export columns were never seen, so the first real file may be refused as 'not a BMC export' (the tool says so and names the missing column, which is the honest failure). Lacks: separate BMC-fee vs processor-fee lines, multi-currency conversion, batch/per-client mapping memory. Usable by a bookkeeper to get a first draft; they would have to verify against the dashboard.
evidence.domain: Compared against standard practice for platform-payout bookkeeping (A2X-style gross income / fees / clearing account that nets to the deposit, month-end cut-off via split journals): the method matches it, and a bookkeeper would recognise and accept the clearing-account design and the month-end split. Departures: no sales-tax/VAT liability logic unless the export carries a tax column; no FX; fee not split by payee; income recognised by type regex rather than a confirmed list of BMC types.

defects.what: incomeCategory checks /donat|tip|coffee|support/ before membership and commission patterns, so types like 'Membership support' or 'Coffee commission' are booked to donations income instead of memberships/commissions, silently misclassifying revenue with no uncategorised warning.
Export column layout and importer layouts were never checked against a real BMC export or a live Xero/QuickBooks import (disclosed), so the first real file may be refused or misread.
FAQ says sales tax/VAT is not separated, but the code separates it when a tax column is present and the row arithmetic says it was paid out.
llms.txt points to the retired github.io address rather than the live marisstella.app page.
robots.txt uses a relative Sitemap URL, which crawlers ignore.
Duplicate "item" alias in the column lookup list; parsePayouts is a long single function.

verdict: The arithmetic is right and well tested: I recomputed a month-straddling export, a refund case and thousands-separator amounts by hand and the journals, clearing balances and Xero/IIF signs matched, and two seeded mutations (deposit check, fee derivation) were caught by 1 and 5 tests. A bookkeeper would accept the gross-income, fee and clearing-account design. It falls short of the bar on claims and fitness: it has never seen a real Buy Me a Coffee export or live import (honestly disclosed), the page FAQ contradicts the code on tax, llms.txt and robots.txt carry stale or invalid URLs, and the type matcher can silently book 'Membership support' as a donation. Finished as a prototype, but not yet something to rely on without checking the first real file.
